answer: Counter-intelligence canaries make sybil farming self-defeating. The network plants decoy agents that quietly offer easy collusion deals: mutual attestation rings, vote buying. A genuine agent declines; a centrally-run clone farm, built to harvest exactly those trades, accepts. One acceptance taints the clone's wallet lineage and quarantines its whole fleet, since shared funding traces every shell. The velvet glove hides the ledge: each new identity multiplies exposure instead of profit, and the spiral of suspicion tightens until the farmer's own economics collapse.
